subject: Non-training assurance: ephemeral artifacts, snapshots, and deletion windows
messages:
From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@finedge.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-20T09:12:00Z
Subject: Quick Q on training and retention for PoC

Mina — thanks again for the demo this morning. Before we move our PoC forward, InfoSec asked for a short write-up on how Redwood handles customer request data. Two quick questions so we can include them in our vendor assessment: 

1) Do you train or fine-tune any of your models on customer request content or logs (explicitly "no training" is what our policy expects)?
2) What retention windows apply to the following artifacts: runtime request logs, debug dumps/snapshots, automated nightly backups, and any persistent caches? Are there any exceptions (legal hold, fraud investigation) that would prevent deletion?

Would also appreciate any supporting artifacts (attestation, SOC2 excerpt) we can attach to the vendor review.

Thanks — if easier we can take a quick call.

—Emma
Emma Liu
Head of Security, FinEdge
emma.liu@finedge.com
Attachments: FinEdge_vendor_questions.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@finedge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-20T11:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick Q on training and retention for PoC

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front: 

1) Redwood does not use customer request content to train or fine-tune models for the hosted service. We have an explicit non-training policy for customer-facing request data in hosted and dedicated deployments (exceptions below).
2) Retention windows differ by artifact; see the bullets below. We can provide an attestation and our SOC2 report excerpt for your packet.

Retention summary (high level):
- Runtime request logs (ingress/egress traces): default TTL 7 days; can be configured shorter for Dedicated/Private. Logs are used for routing, billing, metrics and transient debugging only; training pipelines exclude these logs.
- Debug dumps / ephemeral snapshots (when debug mode is enabled): retained for up to 7 days by default and automatically purged; retention can be shortened on request.
- Nightly backups / snapshots (system-level backups for DR): retained up to 90 days in cold storage for disaster recovery; these are retained encrypted and are not used for model training.
- KV caches / inference caches: ephemeral, typically <24 hours, not persisted to long-term store.

Exceptions: legal holds, court orders, or active fraud investigations may pause deletion for the specific subset of data under hold. Those are documented and handled per our legal process — we notify customers where required.

Next steps: Ben has the exact system names and TTLs; Laura will attach the retention matrix and our playbook. I attached a short playbook and a CSV that maps artifacts to retention windows. We can also generate a signed attestation for your legal team.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Attachments: no_train_playbook_v2.pdf (pdf); retention_matrix_2027-06.csv (csv)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@finedge.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-22T08:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick Q on training and retention for PoC

On Mon, Jun 21, 2027 at 11:04 AM Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Retention summary (high level):
> - Runtime request logs: default TTL 7 days...

Emma — adding the infra specifics so you have actionable items for your security questionnaire: 

- Ingress/egress request logs: routed to transient Kafka topic (topic name: req-trace-prod) with compaction off and retention policy set to 7 days. Consumer jobs aggregate into metrics and then purge. Topic snapshots used for replay are stored <48 hours.
- Debug dumps / developer snapshots: created only when debug flag enabled; placed in an isolated S3 bucket tagged "debug/ephemeral" with lifecycle to delete after 7 days. We do not copy debug artifacts into nightly backups.
- Nightly system snapshots: full filesystem snapshots for DR are pushed to encrypted cold storage (S3 Glacier) and retained for 90 days. These backups are system-level and scrubbed of customer PII pointers; they are not part of any training dataset.
- Model training pipelines: ingestion step explicitly filters out any request logs using the tenant-id exclusion rule (pipeline config: train_ingest_v3 -> filter: tenant_id != customer_tenant_list). We also maintain audit records (deletion-complete events) for retention operations.

Attachments: architect-diagram.png (png) — shows separation of logs vs training pipeline and the filter step.

If you want, we can run a short export showing recent deletion events for your tenant (pseudonymized) so your auditors can confirm deletions occurred.

—Ben
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Emma — absolutely. We can provide a signed attestation (draft attached) that includes the plain-language commitment that customer request data will not be used to train models for hosted services and that retention windows are as noted, subject to legal holds. Our SOC2 Type II report excerpt is available here: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2-report.

Notes on Private deployment: Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments give you full control over retention policies; by default, customer-managed deployments do not send request logs to Redwood-managed training pipelines. We can include a clause in the contract that disallows any mirroring of tenant data into training datasets.

Attached: signed_no_train_attestation-draft.pdf (pdf). I can route a final signed attestation through DocuSign once Procurement confirms the recipient.

Thanks — let me know if Procurement wants the attestation signed by our legal team or a countersigned DocuSign envelope.
